name: Enstrom 280 / F-28
summary: A three-seat piston light helicopter used for training, private flying and light utility work, easily spotted by its three-blade rotor and egg-shaped bubble canopy.

wings: Three-blade fully articulated main rotor on a short, fat mast
Broad-chord blades, noticeably thicker than the thin two-blade rotors on Robinsons
engines: Single piston engine mounted behind the cabin under a rounded cowling
No turbine exhaust stack on the roof
fuselage: Rounded egg-shaped bubble canopy with three seats abreast
One door each side; skids on curved struts
Smooth teardrop pod blends into the tail boom
tail: Tapered tubular boom with a small swept vertical fin
Horizontal stabilizer mounted low on the boom and a two-blade tail rotor

tellTales: Three-blade rotor on a piston-powered bubble-canopy helicopter
Rounded egg-shaped canopy with three seats across and one door each side
Thick, short mast with no tall engine stack on the roof

confusedWith.howToTell: The 280 has a three-blade rotor and a wider three-seat canopy; the R22 has a two-blade teetering rotor, two seats and an exposed engine frame.
Both have three-blade rotors and bubble canopies; the Enstrom has a rounder, bulbous pod with three seats, while the Schweizer 300 has a more open, tapered tail boom and a narrower cabin.
The Bell 47 has a two-blade rotor with a stabilizer bar and an open truss boom; the Enstrom has a three-blade rotor and an enclosed boom.
